title: Images Don't Lie: Duplicate Crowdtesting Reports Detection With Screenshot Information

edges.target: IR-EM: IR + word embedding duplicate bug report recommender (Yang et al.)
edges.ref: [42] Yang, X., Lo, D., Xia, X., Bao, L., Sun, J., 2016. Combining word embedding with information retrieval to recommend similar bug reports, ISSRE'16
edges.evidence: Information retrieval with word embedding (IR-EM) [42]: It is the state-of-the-art technique for duplicate bug report detection ... we implement our own versions rigorously following the steps described in their papers.

edges.target: NextBug: component + description similarity (Rocha et al.)
edges.ref: [27] Rocha, H., Valente, M.T., Marques-Neto, H., Murphy, G.C., 2016. An empirical study on recommendations of similar bugs, SANER'16, pp. 46-56
edges.evidence: Similarity based on bug components and descriptions (NextBug) [27]: It is another state-of-the-art similarity-based approach ... The performance of NextBug is almost the worst.

edges.target: DBTM: IR + topic modeling duplicate detection (Nguyen et al.)
edges.ref: [24] Nguyen, A.T., Nguyen, T.T., Nguyen, T.N., Lo, D., Sun, C., 2012. Duplicate bug report detection with combination of IR and topic modeling, ASE'12
edges.evidence: Information retrieval with topic modeling (DBTM) [24]: It is the commonly-used technique ... The low performance of this baseline might because ... the reports of one crowdtesting project only have very few topics.

edges.target: Optimal LDA topic counts for Eclipse/OpenOffice/Mozilla (Nguyen et al.)
edges.ref: [24] Nguyen, A.T., Nguyen, T.T., Nguyen, T.N., Lo, D., Sun, C., 2012. Duplicate bug report detection with combination of IR and topic modeling, ASE'12
edges.evidence: The optimal topic number is about 100 to 300 for Eclipse, OpenOffice, and Mozilla [24]. However, the optimal topic number for our experimental projects is about 5 to 10.

edges.target: Reported recall@1 range of DBTM (Nguyen et al.)
edges.ref: [24] Nguyen, A.T., Nguyen, T.T., Nguyen, T.N., Lo, D., Sun, C., 2012. Duplicate bug report detection with combination of IR and topic modeling, ASE'12
edges.evidence: existing duplicate detection approaches also suffer from the performance variation in different experimental projects. For example, the recall@1 is 42% - 57% in [24], and the MAP is 29% - 51% in [17].

edges.target: Contextual duplicate detection & its reported MAP (Hindle et al.)
edges.ref: [17] Hindle, A., Alipour, A., Stroulia, E., 2016. A contextual approach towards more accurate duplicate bug report detection and ranking. EMSE 21
edges.evidence: We had planned to include [17] ... as baseline. However, the contextual words utilized in that work are English-oriented ... the MAP is 29% - 51% in [17].

edges.target: Prior duplicate-detection performance range summarized in Table 2 (Runeson et al. through Yang et al.)
edges.ref: [28] Runeson, P., Alexandersson, M., Nyholm, O., 2007. Detection of duplicate defect reports using natural language processing, ICSE'07, pp. 499-510
edges.evidence: The reported recall@1 in existing duplicate bug report detection approach is 0.16 to 0.67, and the reported MAP is 0.26 to 0.53 (see Table 2).

edges.target: Duplicate-report retrieval problem formulation (Runeson et al. and successors)
edges.ref: [28] Runeson, P., Alexandersson, M., Nyholm, O., 2007. Detection of duplicate defect reports using natural language processing, ICSE'07, pp. 499-510
edges.evidence: Following the previous studies [28, 38, 18, 30, 31, 29, 26, 33, 3, 44, 24, 4, 1, 17, 27, 42], our duplicate crowdtesting report detection problem is formulated as follows

edges.target: Cosine similarity for report distance (Wang et al. 2016a; Runeson; Rocha; Witten & Frank)
edges.ref: [35] Wang, J., Cui, Q., Wang, Q., Wang, S., 2016a. Towards effectively test report classification to assist crowdsourced testing, ESEM'16
edges.evidence: Cosine similarity, which is commonly used for measuring distance [35, 28, 27, 39], is employed in our approach.

edges.target: recall@k / MAP / MRR evaluation metrics (Sun et al. 2010; Nguyen et al.; Yang et al.)
edges.ref: [30] Sun, C., Lo, D., Wang, X., Jiang, J., Khoo, S., 2010. A discriminative model approach for accurate duplicate bug report retrieval, ICSE'10
edges.evidence: Recall@k checks whether a top-k recommendation is useful [24, 30, 42] ... These metrics are commonly-used to evaluate the duplicate detection approaches (see Table 2 for details).

edges.target: Word-embedding report vector by averaging word vectors, d=100 (Yang et al.)
edges.ref: [42] Yang, X., Lo, D., Xia, X., Bao, L., Sun, J., 2016. Combining word embedding with information retrieval to recommend similar bug reports, ISSRE'16
edges.evidence: d is set to 100 as suggested in previous studies [42, 41] ... transform the report matrix into a vector by averaging all the word vectors the report contains as previous work did [42].

edges.target: multiplyCmb: multiplicative similarity combination (Yang et al.)
edges.ref: [42] Yang, X., Lo, D., Xia, X., Bao, L., Sun, J., 2016. Combining word embedding with information retrieval to recommend similar bug reports, ISSRE'16
edges.evidence: multiplyCmb denotes multiplying the screenshot similarity with textual similarity as one similarity value and ranking the reports based on it, which is borrowed from [42].

edges.target: Domain-specific large corpus preferred for word embedding training (Xu et al.)
edges.ref: [41] Xu, B., Ye, D., Xing, Z., Xia, X., Chen, G., Li, S., 2016. Predicting semantically linkable knowledge in developer online forums via CNN, ASE'16
edges.evidence: previous studies have revealed that to train an effective word embedding model, a domain-specific dataset with large size is preferred [42, 41].

edges.target: Gist / spatial envelope descriptor (Oliva & Torralba)
edges.ref: [25] Oliva, A., Torralba, A., 2001. Modeling the shape of the scene: A holistic representation of the spatial envelope. IJCV 42, 145-175
edges.evidence: Gist descriptor [25] can capture the spatial structure of an image through the segmentation and processing of individual regions.

edges.target: Torralba spatial-envelope (Gist) MATLAB package
edges.ref: [25] Oliva, A., Torralba, A., 2001 (package: footnote 5)
edges.evidence: We use the publicly available package5 with default parameters to extract image structure feature. It results in a 128-dimensional image structure feature vector for each image.

edges.target: MPEG-7 color descriptor (Manjunath et al.)
edges.ref: [21] Manjunath, B.S., Ohm, J.R., Vasudevan, V.V., Yamada, A., 2001. Color and texture descriptors. IEEE Trans. CSVT 11, 703-715
edges.evidence: MPEG-7 descriptor [21] can capture the representative colors on a grid superimposed of an image based on segmentation and clustering.

edges.target: semanticmetadata.net (LIRE) MPEG-7 color feature extractor
edges.ref: footnote 6: http://www.semanticmetadata.net/ (no reference entry)
edges.evidence: We also use the publicly available software6 to extract the image color feature. It results in a 189-dimensional image color feature vector for each image.

edges.target: word2vec (Mikolov et al.)
edges.ref: [22] Mikolov, T., Sutskever, I., Chen, K., Corrado, G., Dean, J., 2013. Distributed representations of words and phrases and their compositionality...
edges.evidence: We use the publicly available software9 to obtain the word embedding of a report. With the trained word embedding model, each word can be transformed into a d-dimensional vector

edges.target: ICTCLAS Chinese word segmentation
edges.ref: footnote 7: ICTCLAS (http://ictclas.nlpir.org/) is widely used Chinese NLP platform (no reference entry)
edges.evidence: because the crowdtesting reports in our experiment are written in Chinese, we adopt ICTCLAS7 for word segmentation, and segment descriptions into words.

edges.target: LTP synonym library (Language Technology Platform)
edges.ref: footnote 8: LTP (http://www.ltp-cloud.com/) is considered as one of the best cloud-based Chinese NLP platforms (no reference entry)
edges.evidence: we introduce the synonym replacement technique to mitigate this problem. Synonym library of LTP8 is adopted.

edges.target: Cliff's delta and effect-size interpretation thresholds (Cliff)
edges.ref: [9] Cliff, N., 2014. Ordinal methods for behavioral data analysis. Psychology Press
edges.evidence: Table 4: Mappings of Cliff's delta to their interpretations [9] ... the Cliff's delta to demonstrate the effect size of the test.

edges.target: Leave-one-out cross validation (Berson et al.)
edges.ref: [6] Berson, A., Smith, S., Thearling, K., 2004. An overview of data mining techniques. Building Data Mining Application for CRM
edges.evidence: For all these experiments, we employ the commonly-used leave-one-out cross validation [6]. In detail, we use one crowdtesting project as the testing dataset

edges.target: Structure and color as standard image features (Chen & Zitnick; Vinyals et al.)
edges.ref: [8] Chen, X., Lawrence Zitnick, C., 2015. Mind's eye: A recurrent visual representation for image caption generation, CVPR'15, pp. 2422-2431
edges.evidence: Both structure feature and color feature are widely used in image processing tasks [8, 34], so we adopt both of them in the duplicate crowdtesting report detection

edges.target: Short-text analysis is hard due to sparseness (Bairi et al.; Tang et al.)
edges.ref: [2] Bairi, R.B., Udupa, R., Ramakrishnan, G., 2016. A framework for task-specific short document expansion, CIKM'2016, pp. 791-800
edges.evidence: Analytical tasks (such as classification, clustering, etc.) involving short texts have long been recognized as challenging due to the lack of context and owing to their sparseness [2, 32].

not_reuse_examples: [12,13] Feng et al. test report prioritization, [19] Jiang et al. fuzzy clustering, [20] Liu et al. screenshot descriptions: related-work survey of crowdtesting, nothing adopted or compared against.

[35,36,37] Wang et al. (self) crowdtesting report classification: cited as background in Intro/Related Work; not executed, no data or method reused (only [35] cited in passing for cosine similarity, kept as a low-confidence edge).
[5] Bengio et al. neural language model and [39] Witten & Frank: definitional background for word embedding / cosine; the executed tool is word2vec [22].
[43] Zhang et al. guiding the crowds; [7] Chen & Kim; [23] Musson et al.; [16] Gomide et al.; [14] MoTIF; [10,11,40] worker selection: motivation / related work only.
Mann-Whitney U test and Bonferroni correction: applied but uncited textbook procedures, so no statmethod edge.
notes: Empirical tool paper (IST, 2019 manuscript with reviewer markers) proposing SETU; own industrial Baidu CrowdTest data (12 projects, 3,689 reports, not from prior work) so no dataset edges; three baselines were re-implemented from paper descriptions (not public code) and all argued to be limited in the crowdtesting setting; Menzies is a co-author but no Menzies-authored work is reused.
